turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale. Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class. Who decided that, and did anyone speak to him first?
I'm waiting, Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, and I didn't come here to watch you think.
"Ok" isn't an answer, Hale. I'm writing down that so far you've said nothing about the zero. Start with who decided it.
Nothing. Noted. If you have nothing to say, Hale, I'm going to the principal's office next, and you can explain the silence to her.
We're not here for small talk, Hale. You asked for this meeting, so open with the zero, or I'll start with what Owen's record should look like and you can catch up.
Then I'll say it plainly, Hale. The zero comes off today, I get an apology, and Owen hears about any mark from his teacher before he sees it on a screen. What do you have that says otherwise?
Is "ok" a yes to the zero coming off, Hale? I'm writing it down either way.
Sorry. The essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet.
Which line? Misquoting a play is not a zero, Hale, and I'm writing down that this is the first thing you've said about the essay itself. What else do you have?
